name: Euro-area economy
value: Q3 GDP +0.4%; Nov flash composite PMI 51.7
summary: Euro-area flash composite PMI held at 51.7 in November as German growth offset a deeper French downturn
state: The flash eurozone composite PMI was 51.7 in November, unchanged from October, published on 23 Nov (S&P Global). Services eased to a five-month low of 51.2 while manufacturing rose to 52.9; German output grew at its fastest pace since March 2022 and France saw its sharpest contraction in six months (RTE). Eurostat put third-quarter GDP growth at 0.4%, so growth stays positive and the PMI stays above 50.
for_you: The euro-area economy is still growing modestly, with activity uneven between Germany and France. Conditions for jobs and trade across the region are broadly steady for now.
rubric_hit: GDP +0.4% > 0 and flash composite PMI 51.7 > 50 = Normal

sources.title: S&P Global — Flash Eurozone PMI, November 2026
Eurostat — GDP up by 0.4% in the euro area and by 0.5% in the EU
RTE — Euro zone growth holds steady but France clouds outlook

why: The euro area is the UK's largest trading partner; stagnation there hits UK exports and European markets.
drivers: Energy prices, German industry, ECB policy, fiscal rules, China demand.

rubric.alert: Technical recession, or PMI < 45, or bond-spread fragmentation forcing ECB action.
rubric.normal: Positive GDP growth and composite PMI > 50.
